title: Console: 'Lite Cards' compression plan and MVP acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: To meet our Q2 launch constraints and reduce engineering lift, we need a surgically trimmed observability surface for the Console called 'Lite Cards'. This ticket captures scope reductions, rationale, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for dashboards, tracing, and route-level cost breakdown features that will ship in the MVP. Goal: ship a minimal, useful insight set that surfaces customer-impacting signals while deferring lower-value visualizations/features to a follow-up release.
scope_before: Full plan included: 8 dashboard cards (latency P50/P95/P99, throughput, error-rate heatmap, route-level cost breakdown, token-cost waterfall, model variance chart), full trace waterfall with span-level drilldown, adaptive sampling controls, per-route per-token cost attribution, persistent bookmarks, alerts, and long-retention telemetry storage for 90 days.
scope_after: MVP trimmed scope ('Lite Cards'): 4 dashboard cards (latency P95, throughput, error-rate summary, top routes by volume), lightweight route cost summary (aggregate cost per route for last 24h and 7d), simplified trace view that shows sampled request timeline + top 3 spans (no span-level drilldown), no adaptive sampling UI (backend sampling defaults applied), no long-retention UI, bookmarks & alerts deferred.
decisions: 1) Remove span-level drilldown and adaptive sampling controls from MVP to cut UI work and backend indexing effort. 2) Implement aggregated route cost summary instead of per-token waterfall to reduce token-level aggregation compute. 3) Prioritize P95 latency over P50/P99 for initial surface because P95 aligns better with SLO conversations and reduces time-series cardinality. 4) Keep a single retention tier (30 days) for display queries; archive/long-retention work moved to a subsequent release. Rationale: deliver core operational signals for incidents and cost awareness while minimizing infra and frontend complexity.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: 4 cards render on first load within 1.5s for accounts with <10k requests/day and within 3s for accounts up to 100k requests/day.
Latency: P95 latency card reflects data with <5% sampling error compared to raw logs for customers with enabled telemetry.
Cost: Route cost summary shows aggregated cost (USD) per route for last 24h and 7d; values match billing system within 3% for test dataset.
Tracing: Simplified trace view displays sampled request timeline with top 3 spans and a link to raw logs; no span-level editing or drilldown present.
Fallbacks: If backend route-aggregation is unavailable, Console shows an explanatory banner and hides cost cards gracefully (no console errors).
UX: Mobile/tablet view renders condensed cards without horizontal scroll; accessibility checks pass for the new cards (contrast and keyboard focus).
Telemetry: Instrumentation emits 'lite_cards.render' and 'lite_cards.error' events; events appear in analytics pipeline within 15 minutes.
Docs: Short PRD/one-pager and in-console help tooltip are published and linked from the cards before launch.
implementation_notes: Engineering should use existing metrics pipeline and route-mapping service to compute aggregated cost; avoid adding new indices. Frontend: reuse Card component from insights library, but compress visuals to remove sparkline animations. Tracing team: provide a lightweight sampling API endpoint that returns timeline + top spans; avoid heavy span indexing. Ops: cap query window to 30 days for display queries and enforce timeouts (5s) to prevent UI hangs.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated per-account (start internal + beta customers). 2) Week 1: internal dogfood on staging with synthetic traffic; validate performance targets. 3) Week 2: enable for 10% of beta customers, monitor dashboards and error rates. 4) Week 3: expand to 100% of self-serve accounts. 5) Post-launch: collect qualitative feedback and schedule follow-up PRD for span-drilldown and cost waterfall.
comments: 2026-03-11: Scoped down per engineering perf review — removed span drilldown and adaptive sampling UI to meet Q2 launch (Aisha).
2026-03-12: Design delivered compact card mockups; noted need to remove sparkline hover interactions to simplify implementation (Ethan).
2026-03-13: Backend confirmed aggregated cost can be calculated from existing route-mapping DAG with acceptable latency; will add query timeout guard (Maya).
